The towns that kept their bridges

When the motorway came, three river towns refused the bypass. Forty years later, the bill and the benefits are both in.

By Hannah Okoro · 14 min read

In 1984 the county published a plan to route the new road around Aldbury, Wren and Castlemere, and to close the three medieval bridges to traffic. The towns said no. What followed was a decade of hearings, a referendum, and an unusual compromise.

The compromise kept the bridges open to buses, bicycles and deliveries before ten in the morning. Read the full story for the archive photographs and the engineers' reports.

“We didn't save the bridges. The bridges saved the high street.”

Today, footfall in the three towns is twice the county average, and rents have followed. The maintenance budget, meanwhile, has tripled.
